newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nedcor expects 96/97 earnings up 20-30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nedcor expects 96/97 earnings up 20-30 pct.

text.p: Nedcor Ltd, one of South Africa's "big four" banks, said on Thursday it expected to maintain earnings growth of between 20 and 30 percent in the 1996/97 financial year, despite anticipated tough credit conditions.
"I am convinced that we can continue to grow this business into the future at a rate of 20 to 30 percent," Nedcor chairman John Maree said.

Results released on Thursday showed Nedcor earnings surging 30 percent to 502 cents a share, beating analysts' expectations of a 24 percent rise. Net income jumped above the one billion rand level for the first time, up 38 percent to 1.08 billion.
But Richard Laubscher, the chief executive, said the new financial year would be tough on the consumer amid a credit squeeze and slower GDP growth.
"There is no doubt that the prevailing levels of interest rates...are causing discomfort," he said. "The growth rate is also not so robust and asset values have not increased as they should have."
Laubscher said it was difficult to provide an outlook on interest rates as on the one hand a slowdown in the economy pointed to a fall in rates.
"However, (with) the drain on the country's reserves and the possible relaxation of exchange controls interest rates will probably go up."

He said although Nedcor's books were currently positioned for a higher interest rate environment, as they had been in the past year, the bank planned to neutralise its position over the next six to nine months.
